components.name: Lane Badge
components.description: Signature component: a track's side+position (A1, B2…) as a small bordered, ink-numbered chip on an inset fill, instead of plain inline bold text.

narrative.overview: This is an order-intake form for a vinyl pressing plant, and it refuses to look like another SaaS form. It reads as a printed wiring/normalling schedule pulled from a mastering studio's reference binder: white paper, hairline rules, colourless except for one deliberate exception — red, spent only on what needs attention. This is a third pass on the same structural world: an original cream/terracotta identity became a dark 'patch bay' hardware world, which became a fully colourless patch sheet, which now restores exactly one hue (red, warnings/errors/missing parts only) at the user's explicit request. Every other state stays neutral grey or ink.
keyCharacteristics: Pure white ground, near-black ink, no hue anywhere except red, reserved entirely for 'needs attention.'
Severity is binary in hue (neutral vs. red) and reinforced by shape/weight, never color alone.
Panels are divided by a hairline rule, not by background fill; nothing floats on a card.
Tie-line iconography replaces every generic checkmark/exclamation glyph.
Screen and print share one palette — the system was already designed for paper.

rules.name: The One Alarm Rule
rules.body: Red means exactly one thing: something needs attention. Never decorative, never a brand mark, never a positive/neutral state.

rules.name: The Shape-First Rule
rules.body: Wherever red reinforces a state, shape or weight already carries the primary signal (solid-vs-gapped tie-line, bold vs. regular text) — color is the accelerant, not the only mechanism.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No functional on-screen text renders below 11px. Print is exempt as a dense single-page reference sheet read on paper.

rules.name: The Flat, Not Raised Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on any structural element. Distinguish surfaces with a border or a fill tint instead.

dos: Do use red exclusively for warning/error/missing states — reuse the existing tokens, don't invent a second hue.
Do pair red with a shape or weight change wherever practical.
Do keep the tie-line icon vocabulary limited to what the app's data model actually has states for — add new states via pattern, not a new color.
Do reserve monospace/tabular type for genuinely measured or identifying values.
donts: Don't reintroduce the original cream/terracotta identity or the amber patch-bay identity this replaced.
Don't use red for anything that isn't a warning, error, or missing/incomplete part.
Don't add a second hue to match red — solve a new state with shape/weight first.
Don't add a box-shadow to a structural element.
Don't use a Unicode glyph or emoji as a stand-in icon. Every icon is an authored SVG mask.
Don't uppercase a label that reads as a full sentence rather than a short field name.
